source: Approved Layout 4 artifact b9eadbd4-e165-4de9-884d-86acc9fbf2a2 ("SAOC Menu Flyouts"), CSS rules .sheet / .dd4__inner / .dd4__lead / .dd4__col / .dd4__feature / .dd4__feature h4 / .dd4__feature p / .dd4__meta, re-read and grepped verbatim from the published artifact HTML on 2026-09-10. Token values (--rule, --rule-soft, --bone, --muted, --s3..s6) are from the SAME artifact's :root block, also re-verified verbatim on 2026-09-10 against app/globals.css's :root/@theme (colors/fonts all present and Tailwind-reachable; spacing tokens are NOT separately registered but their px values equal the standard Tailwind 4px-scale utilities used below, so no new @theme entry or arbitrary-value syntax is required).
notInScope: The artifact's .container rule (padding: 0 30px, under .proto scope, i.e. prototype-frame-only) is NOT cited here. MegaMenu.tsx's existing outer wrapper (mx-auto max-w-[1280px] px-8) already matches this project's own --container-max/--container-pad tokens (1280px / 32px) and is unrelated to the four gaps below — do not change it. ROUND-3 REGRESSION (2026-09-11): despite this note, @dev's A4 grid-track-ratio edit collaterally dropped px-8 from this same className string anyway, because the horizontal padding and the grid-cols/gap-x-0/pt-8/pb-6 values it WAS supposed to change live in one literal. Fixed by the new e2e assertion 'sheet content keeps a real horizontal inset at <=1280px viewport' (contract A9) — px-8 (or equivalent horizontal inset, on either DOM shape — see A9_ASSERTION_REWRITE_NOTE below) must be restored, nothing else in this wrapper's className should change.
A9_ASSERTION_REWRITE_NOTE: CORRECTION (team lead, 2026-09-11): A9's first implementation measured the GRID element's own bounding box against the panel's bounding box (gridBox.x - panelBox.x). @dev's first fix attempt restored px-8 on that same single grid div and A9 stayed red at 0px — correctly diagnosed as a measurement bug, not a real regression: padding is interior to an element's own box, so a div's own padding can never move that SAME element's boundingBox.x relative to an ancestor. @dev instead used the two-layer alternative (outer `mx-auto max-w-[1280px] px-8`, inner `grid ... gap-x-0 pt-8 pb-6`), which passed A9 as originally written — but that made A9 an assertion on DOM STRUCTURE (which of two divs carries the padding class), not on the visual PROPERTY @qa actually found broken (real rendered content flush against the panel edge). A single-div px-8 form would have fixed the user-visible bug identically and A9 would have wrongly rejected it — the mirror image of this repo's own audited 'assertion satisfiable without the property it claims to prove' defect class, just inverted (unsatisfiable BY a correct property). REWRITTEN to measure the position of real rendered CONTENT against the panel edge instead of a container element's own box: leftInset = the lead eyebrow's ("The National Show", the first rendered content in the sheet — the exact element @qa's regression report measured at x:0) boundingBox.x minus the panel's boundingBox.x; rightInset = the panel's right edge minus the feature rail CTA link's ("Buy tickets", the last rendered content in the sheet) right edge. This is true under EITHER DOM shape. VERIFIED, all three by real command output (2026-09-11): (1) PASSES against the current two-layer tree (`npx playwright test e2e/mega-menu-layout4-visual-fidelity.spec.ts -g "sheet content keeps a real horizontal inset"`, 1 passed). (2) STILL FAILS red against the regression, reconstructed by temporarily stripping px-8 from the real file, running the test, then restoring the file byte-identical from a .tmp/sandbox/ snapshot before and after (never left applied) — `Expected: > 24, Received: 0` on leftInset, same failure signature as @qa's original report. (3) Also MEASURED (not just reasoned) against the single-div px-8 form, reconstructed the same sandboxed-and-reverted way (grid/wrapper divs collapsed into one `mx-auto grid max-w-[1280px] grid-cols-[...] gap-x-0 px-8 pt-8 pb-6` div) — PASSES. The lesson for future assertion authors: constrain the property the bug report actually describes, not the shape of whichever fix happens to land first.

boxShadow.note: Current code uses className `shadow-float`, which app/globals.css:82-83 defines as `0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.04), 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.06)` and whose own comment scopes it to floating menus / nav-on-scroll, not this sheet. shadow-float is also never registered under @theme's --shadow-* namespace (only --color-* and --font-family-* are), so Tailwind v4 does not generate a `.shadow-float` utility from it at all — the class is very likely a no-op today, meaning the sheet may have ZERO box-shadow currently, not merely the wrong one. Do not assume this from theory; the e2e spec below measures the real computed style either way. Fix: replace with an arbitrary-value utility carrying this exact shadow, e.g. shadow-[0_20px_44px_rgba(23,25,23,0.09)].
boxShadow.fragilityNote: app/globals.css:84 defines `--shadow-sheet: 0 20px 44px rgba(23,25,23,.09)` as a literal in :root, and app/globals.css:112 re-declares `--shadow-sheet: var(--shadow-sheet)` inside @theme -- self-referential by name. @qa verified (2026-09-11) the computed style resolves correctly today: this is NOT a defect, because the :root literal is already in the cascade before @theme's own custom-property emission layer resolves var(--shadow-sheet) against it, so it is not a true circular reference in practice. It IS order-fragile, though -- not asserted anywhere structurally, only observed to work. If a future refactor reorders these two declarations, or Tailwind changes how/where @theme emits its custom properties relative to :root, `var(--shadow-sheet)` could resolve to the CSS-wide keyword `unset` instead (an actual circular reference), silently dropping the sheet's box-shadow back to none with no compile-time or lint-time signal -- only the e2e spec's real computed-style assertion (A1, 'sheet: border-top and box-shadow') would catch it, and only by accident of running at all. Recorded as a note for future editors of app/globals.css's :root/@theme block, not a code change against this feature -- the safer pattern (give the @theme key a distinct source name, e.g. --shadow-sheet-value in :root, and have @theme's --shadow-sheet reference that instead of itself) is a candidate for a future cleanup feature, not F7.

innerGrid.selector: the grid element directly containing the lead block, three group columns, and feature rail — currently `div.grid` at components/chrome/MegaMenu.tsx:127
innerGrid.note: Artifact: padding:var(--s6) 0 var(--s5) (32px top / 0 sides / 24px bottom) with NO column-gap property at all — inter-track spacing comes ONLY from each track's own padding plus the border-left on .dd4__col/.dd4__feature, never a grid gap. Current code uses `gap-10 px-8 py-10` (40px gap, symmetric 40px top/bottom, plus 32px horizontal padding baked into the SAME element as the vertical padding) — all three numbers are wrong for this element. --s6=32px and --s5=24px map exactly to Tailwind's default 4px-scale utilities 8 and 6 (pt-8 pb-6) — no arbitrary value needed. Horizontal padding for this grid element itself becomes 0 (px-0); the existing outer max-w-[1280px] wrapper keeps supplying the 32px container margin — see notInScope above.

columnWidthRatios.note: grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1.05fr) minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,.9fr). Current code is grid-cols-[2fr_1fr_1fr_1fr_2fr] — lead and feature rail are both currently DOUBLE the width of a group column and equal to each other; the artifact has the lead only marginally wider (1.05x) and the feature rail narrower (0.9x), not wider. Verify via measured track widths (getBoundingClientRect), not the source literal, since browsers resolve fr into px and this project may render at a narrower effective width than the artifact's own preview frame.

excludes.leadBlock: no border-left — it is the first track, has no left neighbor. .dd4__lead carries only padding-right:var(--s5) (24px), no border rule at all.

trackBorders.note: This is Brad's actual complaint (beta.saoc.co.za screenshots, 2026-09-10 ~21:20: "Menu has no borders"). Current MegaMenu.tsx renders group columns (line ~176) and the feature rail (line ~204) with NO border classes whatsoever.

groupColumns.note: .dd4__col{padding:0 var(--s5)} — 24px left AND right, not just the border side. Current code has no horizontal padding on individual columns at all (spacing came entirely from the now-removed gap-10).

featureRail.padding: 24px (p-6, unchanged from current — this one value was already correct)
featureRail.layout:
natural document flow: meta -> h4 -> blurb

-> CTA , top to bottom, NOT flex+justify-between
featureRail.note: Current code is `flex flex-col justify-between rounded-sm bg-bone p-6` with content split into two flex children (a meta/h4/blurb wrapper div, then the CTA link) so justify-between stretches empty space between them. The artifact's .dd4__feature has NO border-radius property and NO flex/justify-between at all — .dd4__feature p{margin:0 0 var(--s4)} (16px bottom margin) is what creates the gap before the CTA, in normal flow. The large empty grey box in Brad's screenshot is `justify-between` stretching around a MISSING blurb paragraph (see f7-featurerail-blurb.json) — once the blurb renders, remove rounded-sm and justify-between and let the box collapse to content height.

It happens to equal the artifact's .dd-head/.dd-lead-eyebrow letter-spacing (0.18em) exactly, and IS what the eyebrow badge already correctly uses today (tracking-[0.18em] literal) — reuse that same literal or the var, either is correct, just do not invent a different value.
typeTokensVerifiedReachable.tracking-0.14em-dd4-meta: .dd4__meta's letter-spacing (.14em) is a DIFFERENT value from --mono-tracking (.18em) and has no named token anywhere — use the arbitrary literal tracking-[0.14em], never substitute --mono-tracking here.
typeTokensVerifiedReachable.radius-1-not-in-theme: app/globals.css:78 defines --radius-1: 2px (comment: "buttons, inputs") in :root, matching the artifact's .btn border-radius:2px exactly, but --radius-1 is NOT registered under @theme (only --shadow-sheet, --color-*, --font-family-* are, see globals.css:97-116) — Tailwind's bare `rounded-sm` utility does NOT resolve to it (rounded-sm is Tailwind's own built-in scale value, unrelated to this project's --radius-1). Use rounded-[2px] (or rounded-[var(--radius-1)]) for the CTA button, not rounded-sm.
typeTokensVerifiedReachable.font-sans-default-not-mono: the base body font (app/globals.css:132-133) is already var(--sans) — an element with no explicit font-* utility inherits sans, not mono. This matters for leadMetaLine (dd-lead-sub) below, which has no font-family in its own CSS rule and must NOT carry font-mono.

correctionsToTeamLeadsDispatchMessage.ddItemNameColorIsHoverOnly: The dispatch message quoted `.dd-item__name{font-size:14px;font-weight:600;line-height:1.3;color:var(--primary)}` as one rule. Re-grepped the artifact directly (per instruction, not trusting the transcription) and the REAL rule is `.dd-item__name{font-size:14px;font-weight:600;line-height:1.3}` — no color property at all, so it inherits `.dd-item`'s own `color:var(--ink)`. `color:var(--primary)` is a SEPARATE rule, `.dd-item:hover .dd-item__name{color:var(--primary)}` — hover-only. MegaMenu.tsx's current leafLinkClassName already has this exactly right (text-ink base, hover:text-primary) — do not add a base text-primary color to the leaf name, that would be a regression, not a fix. Only font-weight (currently font-bold=700, needs font-semibold=600) and line-height (currently unset, needs leading-[1.3]) are real gaps here.
correctionsToTeamLeadsDispatchMessage.dd1MarginTopOverrideDoesNotApplyToL4: The dispatch message's CSS block included `.dd-head{margin-top:10px}  .dd-head:first-child{margin-top:0}` alongside the base `.dd-head` rule, implying it's part of the shared rule set. Re-grepped: that override is written as `.dd1 .dd-head{...}` / `.dd1 .dd-head:first-child{...}` (artifact lines 77-78) — scoped ONLY to Layout 1 (the single anchored dropdown where multiple headed groups stack in one column, so the 2nd+ heading needs a top gap and the 1st doesn't). Layout 4 (`.dd4__*`) has no equivalent `.dd4 .dd-head` rule anywhere in the artifact. Each L4 group heading (The Show / Visit / Programme / Exhibit & Trade) is already the first child of its own track — no `.dd1`-style margin-top override applies or is needed. The ONE exception is documented under leadBlock.eyebrowAndSecondHeading below: the lead block's SECOND `.dd-head` ("The Show") carries an inline `style="margin-top:20px"` in the artifact's own markup, not a class rule — that is L4-specific and IS required.

groupHeadings.collisionFix: getByRole('heading', { level: 3, name: 'Programme' }) and getByRole('heading', { level: 3, name: 'Tickets' }) [feature rail is h4, level 4, separately] can never match a leaf <a> (role=link) or a <span>/plain text node — the ambiguity in the pre-F7 e2e spec is closed structurally by this element-type change, not by narrowing the query.

outOfScope.mobileMenuDrift: MobileMenu.tsx was explicitly excluded from this feature's scope by the dispatching message. Recorded here as a finding for a LATER feature, not fixed in F7: the artifact's mobile .msub__head (font-mono 9px, letter-spacing .16em, color accent, margin 12px 0 2px) and the inline feature-panel block under .msub (background bone, padding 14px, .dd4__meta reused with an inline margin-bottom:5px override, an inline serif/18px/600/1.15 heading with no shared class name, and a .btn variant with inline padding 9px 14px / font-size 13px) are a DIFFERENT, mobile-specific treatment from every desktop rule cited in this file — do not reuse this file's desktop values for MobileMenu.tsx work; a future feature must re-grep the artifact's mobile markup/CSS independently.
outOfScope.roleMenuMismatch: Recorded per team lead's instruction, not to be fixed here: MegaMenu.tsx's panel uses role="menu" (line ~123) and the trigger uses aria-haspopup="true" (line ~113), which WAI-ARIA APG's Disclosure Navigation Menu pattern explicitly recommends AGAINST for site navigation ('it does not use the WAI-ARIA menu role... No ARIA is better than Bad ARIA', https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/). Changing this touches the disclosure keyboard-interaction contract (arrow-key menu navigation vs plain tab order) and is a bigger surface than this visual-fidelity feature.
outOfScope.futureHeadingLeafCollisionRisk: Recorded per team lead's instruction, not to be fixed here: nothing in nav-config.ts's shape structurally prevents a future leaf label from being renamed to exactly match its own column's heading (as 'Programme' and 'Tickets' already do today). The <h3>/<h4> promotion in this feature closes today's two known instances by construction (role=heading vs role=link can never collide), but a THIRD track's heading and a THIRD track's own leaf could still coincidentally share text with each other's DIFFERENT group in a way that isn't a getByRole collision but IS a getByText collision if a future spec ever reverts to text-based queries — not a live defect today, just a standing trap for future test authors.
